§7.2.5 Highlighted Text

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

text-highlighted-text · text formatting color

✅ Normative

Highlighted text MUST be wrapped in <mark> carrying the highlighter colour as an attribute: <mark style="background-color: yellow">the highlighted phrase</mark>.

Text printed on a highlighter background is content, not decoration. The highlight MUST NOT be dropped, and MUST NOT be reduced to bold or italic.

<mark style="background-color: yellow">the highlighted phrase</mark>

Requirements

  • The colour MUST be named with the nearest HTML colour name — yellow, green, cyan, magenta, lightgray — not a hex value or an invented label. That keeps the vocabulary finite and matches the treatment of colour in Text Colors§7.3.12 and Color as the Value§9.6.4.
  • The <mark> MUST cover exactly the run of text that carries the background. If the highlight stops mid-sentence, so does the <mark>.
  • Inside a table, only the cells whose background is actually coloured are marked; a whole row or column MUST NOT be marked because part of it is highlighted — the same over-application problem as Bold and Italic Inside Tables§9.6.2.

Why keep the colour

In a reviewed document, different highlight colours usually mean different things — one reviewer per colour, or one category per colour. A bare <mark> collapses that distinction and there is no way to recover it afterwards.

Related

  • Text Colors§7.3.12 — the same colour vocabulary for coloured text
  • Bold and Italic Inside Tables§9.6.2 — highlighting inside tables inherits the over-application problem
  • Escaping Printed Marks§7.2.4 — highlighted template placeholders, marked and escaped
